text: Cortisol is now a crowded claim across many aisles, not only supplements. Of the 36 brands studied, coffee swaps (Vahdam, Spacegoods, Everyday Dose), a night-time fat burner (Inno Supps), drink mixes (Calming Co., Nello), a ring (Calmi), men's testosterone brands (Mars Men, Zapply) and a GLP-1 supplement (Zafira) all use cortisol in their ads. Each owns a moment: Vahdam and Spacegoods say your morning coffee spikes cortisol, Inno Supps owns the night-time "cortisol face", Calming Co. owns the evening wine swap. Hormify started a cortisol-first ad on 24 Oct that reached its top 20% on day one. The most common message is still weight: 234 opening lines among the same-product brands, 1.19x the average. "Cortisol detox" as a phrase is used by Harmonia, Her Bodhi, Bioma and a diet app. What this means for AVIA is open; the opportunities below give both readings.

Actual milligrams on screen. Many ads say "clinically studied" or "clinically dosed" (147 same-product openers mention doses, about average), and MUD\WTR discloses its mushroom dose, but no supplement ad we read shows each ingredient's milligrams.

Daytime and the afternoon. Mornings are taken by the coffee swaps ("your morning coffee spikes cortisol") and nights by Inno Supps and Calming Co. Few ads sell the 3 pm wall or the hours between as the cortisol moment.

Women 38–47 in early perimenopause. Most competitor ads speak to 48+ or to men. Everyday Dose and Mira started testing perimenopause in October; Happy Mammoth's "they said I was too young" ads have 10 winners.
Capsules. Most new cortisol brands are drinks or coffee (Vahdam, Spacegoods, Everyday Dose, Nello, Calming Co., Harmonia). Inno Supps is a capsule, but for night-time fat loss.
Being told "it's just stress". Mira's perimenopause ads keep coming back to doctors dismissing women this way. No cortisol brand builds an ad around it yet.
Calm's buyers. Calm's top ads say stress is biology, not willpower, and never say cortisol.
Reviews and a guarantee. Her Bodhi shows neither in 64 ads; most new brands lead with a guarantee (60–90 days), so AVIA would be behind without one.
Don't say "lowers cortisol by X%" or "clinically proven" about the product.
Don't use weight numbers or pound counts, or compare to GLP-1 or Ozempic.
Don't claim to treat menopause, anxiety, insomnia or hot flashes, or to replace HRT.
Don't borrow gut, liver, organ-meat, magnet, testosterone or microbiome claims from other brands.

title: Lead with weight, in AVIA's own way
observed: Weight or belly is the biggest theme by far: 234 opening lines among the same-product brands, 1.19x the average, and 183 of them in the brands' top 20% by impressions (345 ads across all 36 brands).
case_for: It is where buyers respond and where brands spend. AVIA's own copy names stubborn weight first.
case_against: It is the most crowded lane (Hormify, Inno Supps, Harmonia, Calmi all lead with it), weight claims carry the most ad-rejection risk, and MUD\WTR's founder calls fast weight-loss claims "predatory".
test: Same ad body, two openers: weight-first vs symptom-first. Compare hook rate and cost per purchase after about two weeks.

title: Open on sleep, the 3 pm crash or a puffy face
observed: With 36 brands the earlier strong showing faded: sleep and energy openers are now 76 ads at 1.02x (it was 12 ads at 1.90x). Puffy face is 50 ads at 1.11x, but mostly Inno Supps' night-time "cortisol face".
case_for: Less crowded than weight, safer to say, and AVIA's formula covers sleep.
case_against: The bigger sample shows no clear edge, and Inno Supps already owns the puffy face.
test: The same split as above: symptom-first vs weight-first on one ad body.
evidence: claim_check: Sleep, 3 am, tired, energy; Puffy face or bloating

title: Keep saying "cortisol" up front, or lead with the symptom
observed: 82 same-product openers say cortisol, at 0.94x the average; 56 are in the brands' top 20% by impressions. Hormify, Everyday Dose and Calming Co. all moved toward it in the last two months.
case_for: Buyers recognise the word, it is in AVIA's name, and brands keep moving in, which suggests it still pulls.
case_against: So many brands now say it that it may not set AVIA apart, and it scores slightly under average.
test: Two versions of one ad: the first line says cortisol vs the first line names the symptom.

title: Own a moment of the day: the afternoon, or the whole curve
observed: Morning and routine lines are everywhere (264 same-product openers, 0.98x): the coffee swaps own "your morning coffee spikes cortisol". Inno Supps and Calming Co. own the night. Few ads sell the 3 pm wall; Silver Fern alone explains the morning-to-night curve.
case_for: A clear moment is easier to remember and avoids fighting the coffee brands head-on.
case_against: Explaining a curve may be too much for a cold audience, and the morning slot AVIA's capsule fits is the most crowded one.
test: Three openers on one body: morning, 3 pm, and the whole-day curve. Keep what earns the lowest cost per purchase.
evidence: claim_check: Morning or daily routine; money_now (Vahdam, Spacegoods, Inno Supps, Calming Co.)

title: Show the doses
observed: 147 same-product openers mention doses or "clinically studied", about average (1.06x). MUD\WTR wins with a disclosed dose and attacks "proprietary blends"; Spacegoods says "clinically dosed KSM-66". No supplement ad shows every ingredient's milligrams.
case_for: Disclosure is becoming a competitive claim, and AVIA has seven named, dosed ingredients.
case_against: Dose talk performs about average, and buyers may not care about milligrams.
test: Add a 3-second dose card to an ad that already works, vs the same ad without it.
evidence: claim_check: Doses or clinically studied; MUD\WTR, Spacegoods

title: Copy the formats brands spend on
observed: The top ads by impressions across the 36 brands are long story films (Spacegoods' 6-minute gym-dad film, RYZE's 4–11 minute dramas), faceless week-by-week timelines (Zapply #1 of 3,073), talking-cortisol animations (Inno Supps, Zafira), "you said X, so we answered" objection ladders and "we lied" offer reveals (Ultra, Everyday Dose, Spacegoods, Zapply).
case_for: Impressions show where brands put money now, and these formats recur across unrelated brands.
case_against: Formats reflect those brands' budgets and offers; long films are costly, and copying a format many brands use may not stand out.
test: Make one faceless timeline with several openers and one objection ladder; compare cost per purchase over a month.

title: Try buyers from other markets (Calm shows the strongest signal)
observed: Calm's top ads say stress is biology, not willpower ("your nervous system needs a reset"). Goli, RYZE and Thesis now name cortisol in their top ads.
case_for: Huge audiences already taught that stress lives in the body, one step from AVIA's message.
case_against: They bought an app, a gummy or a coffee, not a supplement routine. Nobody has shown these buyers cross over.
test: Add a Calm-style opener to an ad AVIA already runs. Two weeks, with a stop rule set in advance.
